subject: Shared home-office layouts
hook: Built-in or freestanding? It depends how long you'll stay.
ig:
Built-in or freestanding? For a shared office, it mostly depends how long you'll stay.

A: Built-in
Made to the wall, end to end. You get every centimetre of width (often the difference between two desks fitting or not), hidden cable routes and no gaps for things to fall behind. The trade-off: it stays with the house.

B: Freestanding
You can move it, rearrange it or take it with you. The trade-off: standard sizes rarely match your wall, so you lose width at the ends, and the gap behind becomes a cable graveyard.

If you're settled for a few years and two people work in the room, built-in usually wins on space alone.

Which one suits your home right now — and how wide is the wall you'd use? Share it below and we'll tell you how many workstations would fit.
fb:
Sunday question for the work-from-home crowd: built-in desk or freestanding?

Built-in makes the most of a wall and hides the cables, but it stays when you move. Freestanding comes with you, but rarely fits the space exactly, so you lose a bit at each end — and the gap behind soon fills with chargers.

If you're settled for a few years and two of you share the room, built-in usually wins on space alone.

Which would you choose? Tell us the width of the wall you'd use and we'll let you know whether two proper workstations would fit.
